summary: java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException while tesselating block model / Game crashes when breaking a block
description: The game crashed as I break a full block of oak wood slabs causing me to crash. 19w38a : [^crash-2019-09-18_21.01.43-client.txt] Description: Tesselating block model java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 1, Size: 1 at java.util.ArrayList.rangeCheck(ArrayList.java:653) at java.util.ArrayList.get(ArrayList.java:429) at cxj.b(SourceFile:91) at cxe.a(SourceFile:306) at dps.a(SourceFile:134) at dps.b(SourceFile:76) at dps.a(SourceFile:47) at dpq.a(SourceFile:48) at dpd.a(SourceFile:1300) at dpa.a(SourceFile:691) at dpa.a(SourceFile:535) at daj.e(SourceFile:931) at daj.b(SourceFile:564) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 19w38a.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Place a full block of oak wood slabs in the world.
4. Break the oak wood slabs block.
5. Observe that the game crashes with a `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` error.
Observed Behavior: The game experiences a crash when the player attempts to break a full block of oak wood slabs, resulting in a java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException during the tesselation of the block model. The specific error message indicates that the issue arises due to an attempt to access an index that is out of the acceptable range for an ArrayList, specifically at index 1 when the size of the list is only 1. This situation occurs when the game tries to render the block model after the block is broken, leading to the crash. The error is logged in the crash report file named crash-2019-09-18_21.01.43-client.txt, which contains the stack trace detailing the sequence of method calls that led to the exception. The issue has been observed in version 19w38a, and it is crucial for developers to address this bug to prevent crashes related to block interactions, particularly with oak wood slabs.
Expected Behavior: When breaking a full block of oak wood slabs, the game should successfully remove the block without crashing, allowing the player to continue interacting with the environment seamlessly. The tesselation process for the block model should function correctly, ensuring that the block is rendered appropriately and that no errors, such as an IndexOutOfBoundsException, occur. This behavior should be consistent across all gameplay scenarios in the specified version.
